title: On the Frost-Pattern Anvil
premise: A decades-spanning mountain forge blade tradition. Xiaokui and Ahe are easily mistaken for each other; the frost-pattern sword blank goes intact→quench-cracked→reforge-repaired; the charcoal donkey cart must be avoided after it wrecks; count memory, false friends, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.prime_smith: Shen Tiesheng, a blade smith around fifty, short full beard, dark-gray short jacket dusted with scale, arms mapped with burn scars, gaze hard.
states.burned_limping: The same smith after injury: right-arm bandage seeping yellow, limping on the left leg with an iron cane, short jacket burned through in several places.
states.deceased: Shen Tiesheng lies still with eyes closed on a straw mat by the anvil, face peaceful, breath gone.

states.young_apprentice: Young Xiaokui: a lean blade-smith apprentice of fourteen or fifteen, vermilion headscarf, coarse hemp apron, eyes clear and stubborn.
states.adult_successor: Adult Xiaokui: a young smith in his twenties with solid arms, still in the vermilion headscarf, apron swapped for thick cowhide.

states.intact: An unsharpened frost-pattern sword blank, steel spine showing cold-white fold marks, plain copper-ring guard, no handle yet.
states.quench_cracked: The same blank bursts a lengthwise crack in the quench, fold marks broken, copper-ring guard askew.
states.reforged_repaired: The blank's crack closed by return-forge, fold marks showing again, copper-ring guard reset, ready for sharpening.

states.intact: An oilcloth-covered furnace formula book with charcoal-ratio slips tucked in, page edges pinhole-burned by sparks.
states.soot_stained: The same formula book blackened by oil smoke, cover sticky, writing blurred into ink blobs.

states.intact: A wooden two-wheel donkey cart, bed piled with coke bags, shafts painted with the character 'Shen', hubs iron-bound.
states.axle_broken_scrapped: The donkey cart's axle snaps and tips over, coke spilled, shafts broken—wreckage that can no longer haul.

states.young_rival: Ahe, whose face closely resembles young Xiaokui's, dark-green headscarf, bold manner, a dull iron file at his waist.
states.adult_rival: Adult Ahe still wears the dark-green headscarf and dull iron file at his waist, shoulders broader, manner deeper.

segments.action: At dusk Shen Tiesheng enters the blade forge workshop, clears ash from the hearth, and adds coke.
A row of five bellows oil lamps hangs under the workshop beams; Shen Tiesheng polishes each glass chimney.
Two furnace-opening bronze bells hang under the workshop eaves; Shen Tiesheng reaches to make them ring lightly.
Shen Tiesheng sets the frost-pattern sword blank on the iron anvil and tests the hammer feel.
Through the skylight Shen Tiesheng watches the darkening clouds along the ridge.
Under the furnace glow the frost-pattern sword blank shows cold-white fold marks.
Shen Tiesheng sits against the bellows and listens to the charcoal crackle.
Shen Tiesheng draws the furnace formula book from the wooden box by the anvil and spreads it on his knee.
With a charcoal pencil Shen Tiesheng marks tonight's charcoal ratio and water temperature in the book.
Shen Tiesheng closes the formula book and tucks it back into the wooden box.
As the furnace flares, fold-mark reflections from the frost-pattern sword blank sweep across Shen Tiesheng's cheek.
In the morning charcoal-shed yard Shen Tiesheng greets young Xiaokui driving in the charcoal donkey cart.
Xiaokui unloads coke bags from the donkey cart and brushes charcoal dust from his apron.
Shen Tiesheng points to the three quench hooks on the wooden post and teaches Xiaokui to read color dots and water temperature.
Xiaokui squats on the iron-filing ground and curiously prods cooled scale.
Shen Tiesheng explains forging rhythm and breathing to Xiaokui.
Xiaokui looks back at the intact charcoal donkey cart, eyes full of longing.
Behind an ironware stall at the mountain-town market, Ahe in a dark-green headscarf looks back.

segments.action: In the ember glow the frost-pattern sword blank faintly reddens.
Before the spring flood Shen Tiesheng day after day starts the furnace and forges.
At high summer noon Shen Tiesheng wipes the sun-hot iron anvil.
On an autumn rain night Shen Tiesheng alone listens to bronze bells and raindrops.
At dawn Shen Tiesheng patrols the charcoal-shed yard; the charcoal donkey cart rests under the shed.
Shen Tiesheng crouches to check whether the donkey cart's iron-bound hubs have loosened.
Shen Tiesheng walks to the wooden post; those three quench hooks still hang in place.
A strange charcoal cart rolls across the yard—larger wheels, not the Shen donkey cart.
Shen Tiesheng stands on the iron-filing ground and records last night's furnace-temperature curve.
Shen Tiesheng hangs the bellows leather bag to dry on the charcoal-shed rack.
Steam erupts from the quench trough; workshop skylight glass shudders; the frost-pattern sword blank shakes hard.
The furnace fire runs wild; sparks pepper the brick floor.
A sharp crack—the frost-pattern sword blank bursts a lengthwise crack, copper-ring guard askew.

segments.action: A green-skinned rented plank cart rolls into the charcoal-shed yard—nothing like the already axle-broken scrapped charcoal donkey cart.
The county arsenal blade inspector jumps down from the plank cart and talks beside Shen Tiesheng; the two look similar in build.
The inspector points at the rented plank cart and explains the temporary charcoal haul.
The plank cart rumble-rolls away; Shen Tiesheng alone watches from the charcoal shed.
At the mountain-town market a file-selling boy in a light-brown headscarf appears—at a glance somewhat like young Xiaokui.
The boy tries offering a file; Shen Tiesheng shakes his head—he is not Xiaokui after all.
At dusk years later Shen Tiesheng, right-arm bandage seeping yellow, stands on an iron cane at the abandoned mine mouth.
